title: Commands of God
definition: The commands of God are His revealed instructions in Scripture, showing His will and calling His people to faithful love, holiness, justice, worship, and obedience.
summary: God's commands are not burdensome for those made alive by grace; they guide redeemed people in the way of life.
christFocus: Christ fulfilled the law and teaches His people to obey from love, faith, and dependence on Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Commands of God teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to commands of god by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
